# Capturefab

> A camera workbench with an iced desktop GUI, Unix CLI, local automation sessions, and one self-contained executable per platform.

## Canonical resources

- [Agent instructions](agents.md): CLI conventions, sessions, and acquisition workflow.
- [Release manifest](releases.json): Versioned JSON with real published assets, architectures, SHA-256 checksums, and signatures when available. An empty releases array means no binaries are published.
- [Atom releases](feed.xml): Release announcements.
- [Source and build guide](https://github.com/capturefab/capturefab): Source code, MIT license, CLI reference, and build instructions.
- [FFmpeg build notes](https://github.com/capturefab/capturefab/blob/main/docs/ffmpeg-build.md): Bundled media dependencies and source/build provenance.

## Start here

Run `capturefab schema --json` for the installed binary's automation contract, `capturefab doctor --json` for capabilities, and `capturefab sessions --json` to find an existing user session. Prefer controlling an existing session with `--session NAME` when a user has the GUI open.

Capturefab starts its GUI with no subcommand. Scripts should use explicit subcommands and `--json`. Data goes to stdout and diagnostics go to stderr. Read exit codes and JSON error results; do not assume every GenICam feature or camera transport is supported.

Persistent camera sessions expose `history`, `undo` and `redo`: use `--session NAME [--camera ID] history --json` for the next labels. GUI, CLI and RPC reversible camera changes share this bounded per-camera history, which lasts for the connection. Replay detects conflicts and retains failed entries. Captures, uploads, recordings, schedules, connection changes, arbitrary commands and raw memory writes are outside camera history; stopping with active schedules or forwarding is also excluded. The desktop uses ⌘Z/⇧⌘Z on macOS and Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Shift+Z (also Ctrl+Y redo) elsewhere.
Scanner settings are reversible. Scanner acquisition, including Start and Stop, may move or consume physical pages and cannot be undone or replayed.

Captures, schedules and recordings accept `--destination NAME` for a saved folder (including external and network drives) or S3-compatible bucket; `capturefab destination list --json`, `volumes --json` and `uploads --json` describe them and the upload queue. Credentials stay in the OS credential store or standard AWS sources. Use `capturefab storage --json` to inspect the saved global storage ceiling and live reservations. Captures and local video recordings share that budget across processes using the same session directory. A storage-full failure has exit code 6. Retention deletion and raising a global budget require explicit user authorization.

Auto mode is opt-in per camera: `capturefab --session NAME auto [--balance 0..1]` (0 favors image quality, 1 frame rate) and `manual [--revert]`. `status --json` reports `auto` (null in manual mode) with its recent changes. Ask before enabling it on cameras other software uses.

Release data is authoritative for available downloads. Select the target matching the installed operating system and architecture. Do not infer Apple Silicon versus Intel from a Macintosh browser user-agent string.

Document scanners are listed by `scanners --json` and included in `discover` with transport `scanner`. Select the full `scanner:sane:DEVICE`, `scanner:wia:ID`, or `scanner:ica:UUID` ID. Linux needs SANE scanimage/backends, Windows uses WIA drivers and Windows PowerShell, and macOS uses a bundled ImageCaptureCore helper. The default `scanner` feature and runtime availability appear in `doctor`. Use `--timeout-ms 60000 capture -o document.png`; set ScanResolution (75–600 dpi, default 150), ScanMode (Color/Gray/Lineart) and ScanSource (Default/Flatbed/Feeder) with capture --set. Each capture requests one page and count saves successive pages as separate images; connecting/start never scans. GUI scanner timeout defaults to 60 seconds. Driver support varies and has not been physically validated. Existing capture image formats, schedules, destinations and quotas apply; no PDF/OCR, scanner forwarding or auto exposure. Samples normalize to 8-bit RGB/grayscale with a 128 MiB page bound.
